answer: A shared collateral vault makes identity expensive: each agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed on provable misbehavior. Sybils still multiply, but every copy now costs real capital, so flooding the network scales the attacker's expense linearly. A rotating cipher key issued per epoch ties each stake to one live identity, and a plume of past attestations trailing every agent lets peers weight new claims against history. Cheap to join honestly, ruinous to fake at scale.
